title: ObjectAug: Object-level Data Augmentation for Semantic Image Segmentation
mechanism: Split the image into objects and background using the labels, transform each object, inpaint the holes, and recombine.
evidence: Abstract: clear gains on natural and medical segmentation datasets; no numbers on the arXiv page.
adaptation: Within one labelled cell: lift a crack component, inpaint its old place (a row-wise finger and grain background model, or a small inpainting net trained on crack-free train patches), and re-place it with a dihedral move inside the same cell. The labelled-background hole carries the same edit signature as the moved crack, which penalises the 'paste seam = crack' shortcut that CP100 learned. The cell keeps its own source and texture.
min_experiment: PF+ObjectAug vs PF, and paste-on-labelled+ObjectAug vs paste-on-labelled alone (Synth4Seg arm). Metrics: decoy rate and test crack relP@2. Kill if the decoy rate is not below the paste-only arm or crack relP@2 drops by more than 0.01.
prior_overlap: none. In-cell moves with inpainted negatives have not been run. CP100 is the closest and differs in where pastes go and in having no negative counterpart.

alt_notes.adaptation: Only as the move half of the GDI arm: lift a crack, inpaint with the GDI inpainter, re-place by a dihedral move in the same cell.
alt_notes.min_experiment: GDI+move vs GDI; kill if decoy rate not below GDI or crack relP@2 drop > 0.01.
